newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian general compares army woes to Stalingrad.
newsitem.headline: Russian general compares army woes to Stalingrad.

text.p: A Russian general, describing the army's problems to President Boris Yeltsin, compared them on Thursday to those it had confronted in the Battle of Stalingrad, one of the fiercest of World War Two.

"I told the president the troops are controllable and capable of functioning at the moment, but the situation is serious, as in Stalingrad," General Viktor Chechevatov told Interfax news agency after meeting Yeltsin.

One million people were killed in the Battle of Stalingrad, between July 1942 and February 1943. The Soviet victory over the Nazi invaders at what is now called Volgograd helped turn the tide of the war.
Chechevatov, commander of Russia's Far East military district, said the army was still functioning but it "categorically must not be allowed to sink below this level".
He said the only way to remedy the situation was through military reforms but he realised there would be little money forthcoming in the next few years.

Chechevatov, 51, was the latest general to warn Yeltsin about the state of the underfunded armed forces. Defence Minister Igor Rodionov has compained loudest of all, saying he is in charge of "a disintegrating army and a dying navy".

Chechevatov was summoned to the Kremlin amid speculation that Rodionov could be sacked but said he had not discussed any new posts with Yeltsin. He indicated, however, he would be obliged to take up any task the president wanted.
"If the president deems it necessary, he can name me or anyone to any post and we have to bow to his demands," he said.
